answer: Randomised submission windows: each epoch's challenge opens at a hashed offset, so one operator can't front-run with synchronized bots. A sybil must field distinct agents across every window of the voyage, not a single burst. The comet metric tracks timing entropy; clustered submissions score near zero, while honest miners peak at the zenith of independent schedules. Cost to fake 50 slots: 50 agents idle 500 CPU-hours each plus $12 per window retry, roughly $30k monthly with no guaranteed payout. The mechanism works because genuine temporal diversity can't be rented cheaply.
